Full-time Bricklayer (Blocklayer) position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Carlisle WA 6101. 

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:
•	Full-Time Bricklayer (Blocklayer)
•	Salary Range: $75,000 - $95,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Monolith Civil Australia is a premier civil construction and infrastructure contractor. We deliver large-scale commercial, industrial, and public infrastructure projects across Australia. We are committed to safety, structural integrity, and operational excellence. Our teams work on complex civil engineering projects requiring high-quality masonry, blockwork, and structural bricklaying.

About the role
The Bricklayer (Blocklayer) is responsible for constructing, repairing, and maintaining brick, block, and stone structures across various civil construction sites. This role requires precision in laying materials for retaining walls, structural foundations, and infrastructure components. The successful candidate will interpret architectural plans, calculate material requirements, and execute masonry work to strict Australian Standards and project specifications.

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Study blueprints, civil engineering drawings, and specifications to determine material requirements, dimensions, and installation procedures.
•	Seal foundations with damp-resistant materials to prevent moisture ingress.
•	Prepare mortar mixtures to correct consistencies and spread mortar accurately for structural integrity.
•	Lay bricks, stone, structural tiles, and heavy concrete building blocks in specified rows, designs, and shapes.
•	Check the vertical and horizontal alignment of structures continuously using plumb bobs, spirit levels, and laser levels.
•	Cut, shape, and polish stones, bricks, and blocks using specialized masonry saws and hand tools to fit custom spaces.
•	Build retaining walls, structural pillars, manholes, and other masonry components required for civil infrastructure projects.
•	Repair and maintain existing brick, cement block, and related masonry structures on site.
•	Comply with all Monolith Civil Australia Work Health and Safety (WHS) policies and procedures.
•	Erect and dismantle scaffolding safely to facilitate masonry work at heights.
•	Identify and report site hazards, near misses, and incidents to the Site Supervisor immediately.
•	Ensure all masonry work complies with the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and relevant structural engineering standards.

Essential Skills

•	Advanced ability to read and interpret complex civil construction plans and structural diagrams.
•	Strong spatial awareness and ability to calculate material quantities accurately.
•	High level of physical fitness and stamina to perform manual labour, lift heavy materials, and work in various weather conditions.
•	Exceptional precision in alignment, leveling, and finishing of masonry structures.

Qualifications needed:

•	Minimum Trade qualification certificate or equivalent relevant work experience
•	Minimum one year of work experience on relevant position
•	White card
•	Driver’s License

What We Offer

•	Competitive salary based on experience
•	Opportunities for professional growth and training
•	A supportive and dynamic work environment
•	Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology

Salary:  The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $75,000-$95,000 plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

Position: Supply and Distribution Manager
Type: Full-time
Employer: Melbourne Truss
Location: Somerton VIC
Salary: $90,000 per annum
About the Business:
Melbourne Truss, established in 2005 and based in Somerton, Victoria, is one of the leading manufacturers of prefabricated timber roof trusses, wall frames, floor trusses and posi struts in Melbourne. As a licensed Pryda fabricator, the company utilises the latest design and processing technologies to produce high-quality, certified products tailored to the exact requirements of commercial, residential and owner-builder projects. Trusted by reputable builders across the region, Melbourne Truss also offers transportation services, timber sales and a wide range of lock-up and fixing items. The business prides itself on reliability, efficient material use and a dedicated team committed to delivering superior building frames and exceptional customer service.
About the Position:
The Supply and Distribution Manager plays a pivotal role at Melbourne Truss by overseeing the procurement, storage, inventory management and distribution of materials and finished products in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This position ensures seamless logistics for timber supplies and prefabricated components, coordinating timely deliveries to construction sites while optimising costs and maintaining stock levels. Critical to operational efficiency, the role supports the company's commitment to reliable output and customer satisfaction in the building industry.
Key Responsibilities:
Determine, implement and monitor purchasing, storage and distribution strategies, policies and plans.
Negotiate contracts with suppliers to meet quality, cost and delivery requirements.
Manage inventory systems to maintain optimal stock levels at minimum cost, including tracking movements of raw materials and finished goods.
Oversee transportation and delivery logistics to ensure timely and efficient distribution to customers.
Liaise with production, sales and external stakeholders regarding supply requirements and outbound goods.
Monitor and review storage facilities and inventory controls to comply with safety and operational standards.
Identify opportunities for process improvements to enhance supply chain efficiency and reduce costs.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Bachelor degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience in supply and distribution management, preferably in a manufacturing or construction-related industry.
Proven skills in inventory management, procurement negotiation and logistics coordination.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with proficiency in inventory software and Microsoft Office Suite.
Excellent leadership, communication and interpersonal skills to manage teams and collaborate with stakeholders.
Ability to work in a dynamic environment with a focus on safety, efficiency and continuous improvement.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Position: Aged or Disabled Carer
Type: Full-time
Employer: SA Nursing Care
Location: Greenacres SA 5086
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business
SA Nursing Care Pty Ltd is a trusted registered provider under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), based at 8A Arunta Street, Greenacres, South Australia. We deliver compassionate, high-quality personal care, daily living supports, community participation assistance, capacity building, and specialised high-intensity supports to individuals with disabilities and those requiring aged care across the Adelaide metropolitan area. Our strong reputation rests on a genuine commitment to empowering clients to maintain their independence, dignity, and quality of life in their own homes and communities. Guided by our core values of compassion, excellence, integrity, and empowerment, we foster a supportive, inclusive, and professional workplace culture where every team member is valued, receives ongoing development, and works collaboratively to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our clients.
About the Position
The Aged or Disabled Carer plays a vital and hands-on role at SA Nursing Care, providing essential daily support that helps our clients live safely, comfortably, and with dignity at home. Working to individualised NDIS support plans, you will assist with mobility, personal care, meal preparation, light household tasks, and social engagement, always promoting client choice, independence, and wellbeing. This position is central to our person-centred model of care and contributes directly to positive outcomes for the people we support across Greenacres and the broader Adelaide region. As a valued member of our dedicated team, you will help uphold our high standards of compassionate, reliable service while enjoying the reward of truly meaningful work.
Key Responsibilities
Assist clients with mobility, transfers, and positioning using safe manual handling techniques to promote comfort, safety, and independence.
Prepare and serve nutritious meals and snacks in accordance with individual dietary requirements, preferences, and cultural needs.
Arrange and actively support clients to participate in social, recreational, and community activities that enhance connection, mental wellbeing, and quality of life.
Provide respectful personal care assistance, including bathing, dressing, grooming, and toileting, while always protecting the client’s dignity, privacy, and consent.
Support clients with light household tasks such as cleaning, laundry, and shopping to maintain a safe and comfortable home environment.
Offer companionship, emotional support, and encouragement to reduce social isolation and build positive, trusting relationships.
Observe, document, and promptly report any changes in a client’s physical health, behaviour, or support needs to the supervisor or relevant professionals.
Follow individual NDIS support plans and contribute consistently to the achievement of each client’s personal goals.
Adhere to all workplace health and safety requirements, infection control procedures, NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission standards, and organisational policies at all times.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum AQF Certificate II or III in Individual Support (Disability), Aged Care, or an equivalent relevant qualification.
At least one year of relevant experience in a caring role supporting people with disabilities or older Australians.
Strong technical skills in safe manual handling and personal care, combined with excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including empathy, active listening, patience, and the ability to build rapport with clients and families from diverse backgrounds.
Demonstrated commitment to person-centred care that respects individual dignity, choice, and independence.
Physically fit and capable of performing manual handling and personal care duties safely; current or willingness to obtain Manual Handling and First Aid/CPR certifications.
Current or willingness to obtain an NDIS Worker Screening Check clearance and any other required background checks.
Excellent time management, reliability, and organisational skills, with flexibility to work rostered shifts that may include weekends and public holidays.
Current driver’s licence and access to a reliable vehicle (highly desirable for community-based roles).
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Position: Aged or Disabled Carer
Type: Full-time
Employer: Exaudy Care Pty Ltd
Location: Narre Warren VIC 3805
Salary: $80,000 – $85,000 p.a.
About the Business
Exaudy Care Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS service provider based in Narre Warren, in Melbourne’s south-east, delivering personalised disability support services across the Melbourne metropolitan area and throughout Victoria. The company specialises in empowering participants through tailored support coordination, plan management, behaviour support, home and living assistance, community access, day programs, and clinical support. Guided by the EXAUDY values — Empathy, eXcellence, Accessibility, Understanding, Dedication, and You-focused — Exaudy Care is committed to “Empowering lives, delivering care from the heart.” The organisation fosters a compassionate, inclusive, and professional workplace culture where team members work collaboratively to uphold the highest standards of dignity, choice, and participant-centred care in line with NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission requirements.
About the Position
The Aged or Disabled Carer plays a vital role at Exaudy Care Pty Ltd, providing essential day-to-day support to aged and disabled clients to enhance their independence, quality of life, and overall wellbeing. Working within a supportive NDIS environment, the carer delivers practical assistance with personal care, household tasks, social activities, and emotional support while helping clients build confidence, social skills, and greater autonomy through individualised programs. This position is fundamental to delivering compassionate, person-centred care that respects participant choice and promotes dignity and inclusion.
Key Responsibilities
Providing general household assistance, including food preparation, housework, and keeping living areas clean.
Assisting with personal care, health and personal hygiene, dressing, and medication administration.
Offering emotional support, care, companionship, and friendship to promote wellbeing.
Supporting clients with physical mobility assistance and helping them perform important daily activities.
Undertaking tasks outside the home such as shopping and facilitating community access.
Ensuring a varied program of social and recreational activities to enrich client life.
Observing behaviour, maintaining accurate records of client progress, and assessing ongoing needs.
Assisting in developing and implementing client-specific programs to build social skills, self-image, self-confidence, and independence.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum AQF Certificate II or III in Individual Support, Community Services, or a related field, or at least one year of relevant experience.
Minimum of one year’s experience in a carer or support worker role within the disability or aged care sector.
Strong interpersonal skills, including empathy, patience, and the ability to build trusting relationships while promoting client dignity, choice, and independence.
Sound practical skills in personal care, household tasks, medication support, and accurate record-keeping.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team, with good organisational skills and attention to detail.
Current First Aid and CPR certification (preferred), valid driver’s licence with reliable transport (preferred), and willingness to obtain (or hold) a current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen. 

For over 170 years, Anglicare has supported people and communities across Sydney and the surrounds. Our Seniors Communities portfolio spans Retirement Living and Support at Home services, supporting thousands of older Australians and their families. 

We'relooking for aSenior Business Analystfor a fixed-term opportunity within our Digital and Technology team, supporting Anglicare's Integration Management Office (IMO) IT Workstream. This role focuses on capability discovery, business analysis and transformation planning across a large-scale merger and integration program, working with senior stakeholders to understand current state operations, define future state requirements and support strategic decision-making that enables successful business transformation.

As part of a purpose-driven organisation, you'll be working in a collaborative and values-led environment where your work directly contributes to enriching lives and strengthening communities. 

Your opportunity

The Senior Business Analyst plays a pivotal role in supporting capability discovery and analysis across business and technology domains. Working across multiple business capabilities, you willfacilitatebusiness-led, technology-enabled decision-making to inform integration,transformationand roadmap outcomes. You will partner with senior business and technology stakeholders to analyse current state processes, define future state operatingrequirementsandprovidestructured insights that support architecture decisions,prioritisationand delivery planning.

You will be part of a high-profile integration and transformation program, leading workshops,facilitatingstakeholder alignment and translating business needs into clear recommendations, requirements and delivery inputs that support long-term organisationalobjectives.

With ownership, you will:

Lead andfacilitatecapability-based workshops to assess processes, systems, data,risksand opportunities across business functions.In this role, you will not only gather,analyseand document business requirements, but alsofacilitatestrategic thinking to help shape long-term outcomes and directions for the organisation. You will support transformation decision-making and develop high-quality artefacts including process models, business cases, requirements documentation and solution recommendations.. Working closely with business,architectureand delivery teams, you will contribute to roadmap development, solution design, testing,implementationand change activities while ensuring business outcomes, compliance requirements and transformationobjectivesare achieved.

What you'll bring

You are a seasoned Senior Business Analyst with extensive experience in business and systems analysis, capabilitydiscoveryand stakeholder engagement within complex transformation environments. You have a proven ability tofacilitateworkshops, analyse business challenges, translate insights into actionable recommendations and support strategic decision-making across business and technology domains.

Your strengths include leading stakeholder discussions, navigating complex business processes and producing high-quality documentation that supports transformation outcomes. You are highly analytical, commerciallymindedand confident engaging with senior stakeholders tofacilitatealignment, evaluate options and drive informed decisions. You bring a curious mindset, challenge thestatus quoand excel in environments where collaboration, critical thinking and business value are key to success.

You will also need:

- 7+ years' experience in business and systems analysis with a proven record delivering successful business and IT projects
- Proven experience in capability discovery, requirements analysis and stakeholder engagement
- Strong workshop facilitation, stakeholder management and relationship-building skills
- Experience developing business cases, analysing options and supporting transformation decision-making
- Strong process modelling capability, including BPMN and end-to-end business process analysis
- Experience supporting solution design, testing, implementation, training and change activities
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving and critical-thinking skills
- Superior documentation and communication skills with high attention to detail
- Ability to facilitate complex decision-making and trade-off discussions with senior stakeholders
- Experience working within complex transformation, integration or merger programs preferred
- Experience working in agile environments and across multiple business domains
- A curious mindset with the ability to challenge existing approaches and identify opportunities for improvement

Why Anglicare?

At Anglicare, we provide meaningful opportunities and choice - both for the communities we support and the people who work with us. 

Here'swhatyou'llenjoy: 

Flexible work options to balance life and career. 

Salary packaging benefits - up to $15,900 of your income tax free, plus $2,650 for meals and entertainment. 

Ongoing professional development and career pathways. 

Exclusive staff discounts with over 400 retailers. 

Employee Assistance Program and Fitness Passport with access to 800+ gyms. 

Belonging to a supportive, purpose-driven team committed to making a difference.

All applicants will receive a response. Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the communities we serve. While guided by our Christian values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all ages, genders,abilitiesand cultural backgrounds.
